subject: English
passage: Tanaka and Yamamoto et al. have confirmed that fifteen plant species (including Acacia tortilis and species from the genus Prosopis) maintain elevated hydrostatic pressure in both their aerial shoots and their root systems (the network of root hairs from which the shoots emerge), though the benefits of this hyperhydric behavior are unclear. Noting that relative pressure elevation was more pronounced in xylem-associated than in non-transporting regions of the root system—a difference that persisted even after aerial shoots were pruned—the researchers speculate that osmoregulation in the root system may influence drought survival.
prompt: Which statement about the root systems of the fifteen plant species is best supported by the text?

choices.A: The root systems generally maintain pressure levels lower than those of the aerial shoots even when considering pressure variations between xylem-associated and non-transporting regions.
choices.B: The correlation between higher root system pressure and greater drought resistance indicates that successful survival may be dependent on osmoregulation in the root system.
choices.C: Variation in osmoregulation across the root system may occur independent of the presence or absence of aerial shoots.
choices.D: Pressure levels in the xylem-associated areas of the root system are higher than in the non-transporting areas due to differences in the depth and lateral spread of the roots within soil or other growth media.

explanation: Choice C is the best answer because it accurately represents what the research findings support. The text states that pressure elevation was more pronounced in xylem-associated than in non-transporting regions of the root system and that this difference persisted even after aerial shoots were pruned. This experimental finding demonstrates that the variation in osmoregulation across the root system continued to exist even when the aerial shoots were removed, providing direct evidence that root system osmoregulatory variation can occur independently of whether aerial shoots are present or absent.
